title: Check yourself: monitors and synchronized blocks

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A report class has `synchronized void render() { header(); body(); }` and `synchronized void header() { ... }`, both instance methods. One thread calls render() on a report that no other thread is using. What happens when render() calls header()?

options.text: header() runs, since the thread already owns the report's monitor and may enter it again
options.says: a monitor is reentrant: its owner enters again, the count goes up, and others can enter only at zero

options.text: header() runs, since a synchronized method called from another one on the same object skips the monitor
options.says: header() does take the monitor; it succeeds because the monitor is reentrant, not because the call skips it

options.text: The thread waits for good, since header() needs the monitor that render() has not yet released
options.says: the monitor is reentrant, so its owner never waits for itself

options.text: The thread waits for good, since one thread can own only one monitor at a time
options.says: a thread can own several monitors, and the same one several times

origin.section: Each Synchronized Method Is Atomic; a Check Followed by an Act Is Not

questions.stem: A directory has `synchronized void rename(String from, String to) { Entry e = byName.remove(from); checkName(to); byName.put(to, e); }` and a synchronized lookup(name). checkName throws IllegalArgumentException for a blank name. One thread calls rename("ops", ""); after it has failed, another thread calls lookup("ops"). What does that thread get?

options.text: It gets no entry, since the monitor was released with the entry removed and not put back
options.says: the exception released the monitor; the remove before the throw stays, and the next thread sees it

options.text: It gets the ops entry, since leaving a monitor by an exception undoes what the block changed
options.says: the release undoes nothing; writes made before the throw stay

options.text: It never returns, since the renaming thread still owns the monitor after its exception
options.says: a synchronized method's monitor is released however the method completes, exceptions included

options.text: It never returns, since a monitor left by an exception stays held until the JVM clears it
options.says: the monitor is released as the exception leaves the method; nothing stays held

origin.section: The Monitor Is Released However the Block Exits, Half-Done Changes Included

questions.stem: A quota class keeps `private static int used`. Request threads call `synchronized void consume() { used++; }` on the one shared instance, and a nightly job calls `static synchronized void reset() { used = 0; }`. Can reset() run while a request thread is inside consume()?

options.text: No, since reset() and consume() are synchronized members of one class and so share its lock
options.says: the keyword sits on the methods, but they lock different objects: the instance and the Class object

options.text: No, since reset() locks the Class object, and that lock also covers the instance consume() locks
options.says: a static synchronized method locks only the Class object, a different object from the instance

options.text: Yes, since reset() locks the Class object and consume() locks the instance, two different objects
options.says: two different monitors exclude nothing from each other, so both can touch used at once

options.text: Yes, since reset() is static and so takes no lock, while consume() locks the instance
options.says: it takes the monitor of the class's Class object

origin.section: synchronized Locks an Object, and Excludes Only Code That Locks the Same One

questions.stem: A connection pool uses one monitor. borrow() runs `while (free.isEmpty()) wait();` and drain() runs `while (free.size() < total) wait();`. An admin thread is waiting in drain() and a request thread in borrow() when another thread returns one connection, leaving one of two free, and calls notify(). The request thread goes on waiting although a connection is free. Why?

options.text: The admin thread was woken, found its own condition still false, and waited again
options.says: notify() wakes one arbitrary waiter; the admin thread re-checked, waited again, and the notification was spent

options.text: The admin thread was woken, and it keeps the notification until its own condition is true
options.says: a thread that waits again keeps nothing; the notification is spent

options.text: No thread was woken, since notify() does nothing while some waiter's condition is still false
options.says: notify() wakes one waiter whatever the conditions; each waiter checks its own condition after waking

options.text: No thread was woken, since notify() reaches waiters only after the notifying thread has ended
options.says: notify() wakes a waiter, which is then BLOCKED until it gets the monitor back, as the woken packers show; nothing waits for the notifying thread to end

origin.section: wait() Belongs in a Loop Over Its Condition, and a Change Is Announced With notifyAll()

concepts: With waiters for different conditions on one monitor, notify() can leave a thread waiting although its condition holds.
A monitor is reentrant: its owner can enter it again, so a synchronized method can call another one on the same object.
A static synchronized method locks the Class object and an instance one locks this, so the two exclude nothing from each other.
